findings.what: 10 consecutive zig build test runs at HEAD (307ec4c): all 10 passed (exit 0), mean wall time 39.9s (range 39.6-40.3s). Zero build-step failures, zero test failures. Serial run (-j1) also passed (45.1s).

The previously observed flakiness (T314: 390/393 → 393/393 with 1 build step failing) did not reproduce. Likely causes at b3d0209: dirty tree (the binary was -dirty stamped), concurrent zig build processes contending for .zig-cache, or filesystem pressure from parallel builds.
findings.denominator: 0 failures in 10 parallel runs + 1 serial run = 0/11 observed failures

findings.what: Proposed fix: if the flakiness recurs, the most likely root cause is .zig-cache contention during parallel zig build. The suite already runs tests via addRunArtifact (pre-built test binaries), which should not contend. If build-step failures persist, isolate by running regression scripts sequentially and test binaries in parallel (zig build test runs all steps in dependency order, but regression scripts under tools/ may race on shared /tmp fixtures).
